entries.title: Human anatomy and organ systems overview
entries.summary: MedlinePlus (U.S. National Library of Medicine) defines anatomy as the study of the body's structure, organizing reference resources across cardiovascular, respiratory, nervous, digestive, musculoskeletal, endocrine, immune, and urinary systems.

entries.title: DNA, chromosomes, and the human genome
entries.summary: Per NIH NHGRI, DNA is a double helix built from four nucleotide bases (A pairs with T; C pairs with G). The human genome comprises roughly 3 billion base pairs and an estimated 20,000 to 25,000 genes organized on 23 pairs of chromosomes in the cell nucleus.

entries.title: First aid overview and emergency 911 guidance
entries.summary: MedlinePlus defines first aid as immediate care provided for an injury or sudden illness before medical help arrives, emphasizing calling 911 for life-threatening emergencies (or U.S. Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222) and maintaining basic kit supplies. Educational overview only; not personal medical advice.

entries.title: Public health statistics (WHO GHO and CDC FastStats)
entries.summary: WHO's Global Health Observatory and CDC's National Center for Health Statistics (FastStats) publish population-level health indicators covering mortality, life expectancy, infectious disease surveillance, and health care utilization.
